label: Section 338: 50% tariffs take effect on $20B of Canadian goods
notes: Proclaimed Jul 20, 2026; paused Aug 18; took legal effect 12:01am ET Aug 22 after talks collapsed — covers electronics, plastics, wood, paper, dairy, alcohol, cement, clothing, hockey equipment; no USMCA exemption; energy, potash, fish, critical minerals exempted

label: Section 232: 50% steel & aluminum tariff
notes: Hamilton, Ontario steel sector hit hardest; doubled from 25% in Jun 2025

label: 10% baseline tariff on non-USMCA Mexican goods
notes: USTR proposed the additional 10% Jun 2, 2026, then gave it concrete effect via a Section 301 forced-labor tariff implemented Jul 24, 2026; Mexico contested via negotiation, not retaliation, and is now pressing for parity with Canada's draft deal terms

label: Auto & auto-parts tariff exposure
notes: Central rules-of-origin dispute; industry pushing for sub-6% effective rate

label: Ontario cross-border electricity flow
notes: Site of the brief Mar 2025 25% export surcharge to Michigan, New York, Minnesota

label: Gordie Howe Bridge trade corridor
notes: $274M+ in daily trade; 30% of Canada-US truck trade by volume

label: Ambassador Bridge trade corridor
notes: Longstanding primary crossing, now sharing volume with the new Gordie Howe bridge

label: Laredo-Austin trade corridor
notes: Largest US-Mexico land port of entry by trade value

label: US-Mexico bilateral negotiating track
notes: Third round concluded Jul 24; fourth round scheduled Sep 2026 in Washington

label: US-Canada trade talks collapse
notes: Talks broke down late Aug 21, minutes before the Aug 22 00:01 ET deadline. Carney suspended negotiations and recalled Canadian negotiators, citing unfair last-minute US terms; Greer said Canada walked back agreed commitments. USTR: no new talks currently planned.

label: Canada's retaliation finalized: C$27.6B, sliding 15-50% scale, effective Sep 8
notes: Aug 25: Champagne, Joly, Hajdu and Solomon detailed the finalized package — sliding 15/25/50% tariffs on C$27.6B of US goods (steel, aluminum, dairy, furniture, cosmetics, smartphones, seafood, appliances, textiles) plus a C$7.5B worker/business support package with EI expansion, taking effect Sept 8, 2026. Supersedes the Aug 22 dollar-for-dollar framing.

label: Trump threatens 50% auto/truck/steel tariffs from Jan 1, 2027
notes: Truth Social post told Canada to 'fall in line' or face consequences 'far WORSE,' threatening new 50% tariffs on vehicles, trucks, auto parts and steel starting Jan 1, 2027; Trump referred to Carney as 'Governor Carney.' Carney rejected the framing as treating Canada 'as a subsidiary of the United States.'

label: SCOTUS strikes down IEEPA tariff authority
notes: 6-3 ruling in Learning Resources v. Trump forced pivot to Section 122/232/338

label: $166B IEEPA refund remand proceedings
notes: US Court of International Trade handling refund claims after SCOTUS ruling

label: Keystone XL pipeline revival proposal
notes: Floated by Trump as a possible component of the Aug 19 framework deal

label: Softwood lumber tariff dispute
notes: Long-running dispute absorbed into Section 232 lumber, cabinet & furniture tariffs

label: Dairy market access dispute
notes: US dairy exporters seeking expanded access to Canada's supply-managed system
